title: alpha7 integrin co-regulates chromatin accessibility and gene expression in HPV-negative head and neck cancer.
authors: Borodins, Olegs; Vehlow, Anne; Sameith, Katrin; Dahl, Andreas; Spangle, Jennifer M; Aust, Daniela E; Brunner, Cornelia; Monni, Outi; Lange, Inga; Mircetic, Jovan; Thomas, Elisa; Cordes, Nils
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合多组学与AI分析，发现alpha7整合素通过AURKA轴调控染色质可及性和基因表达，但核心对象是癌症信号通路而非染色质三维空间架构建模，方法上AI仅用于特征选择，缺乏三维基因组结构建模。
abstract: Epigenetic regulation and gene transcription are dynamically modulated by extracellular signals, including focal adhesions; however, the role of integrins in these processes remains poorly understood. In this study in HPV-negative head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, (HNSCC), we combined investigations in physiological three-dimensional, matrix-embedded cell models and patient-derived organoids with multi-omics analyses, bioinformatics and artificial intelligence, to unmask the integrin effector signaling network that reshapes chromatin to drive cancer. Among the 12 alpha/beta1 integrin receptors, alpha7 integrin (ITGA7) emerged as the most potent modulator of histone post-translational modifications, associated with significant changes in gene transcription and chromatin accessibility. Depletion of ITGA7, achieved independently by CRISPR/Cas9 knockout and RNA interference, reduced chromatin accessibility at the AURKA locus and downregulated an AURKA-centered transcriptional program. Mechanistically, phosphoproteomics revealed significant inhibition of MAPK- and PI3K/AKT-dependent signaling with concomitant functional impairment of cell cycling and cell survival upon ITGA7 depletion. Across all analyses, machine-learning-based feature selection consistently nominated AURKA as the dominant downstream node, and tumor ITGA7 expression stratified patient overall survival in a non-linear manner. In summary, these findings establish alpha7 integrin as a key co-regulator of chromatin accessibility and gene transcription in HPV-negative HNSCC, acting through an AURKA-centered axis that couples adhesion signaling to cell cycle control and patient survival, and nominate AURKA, potentially targetable with clinical Aurora-A inhibitors such as alisertib, as an actionable therapeutic node downstream of the currently non-druggable ITGA7.
abstract_zh: 表观遗传调控和基因转录受到包括黏着斑在内的细胞外信号的动态调节；然而，整合素在这些过程中的作用仍知之甚少。在本研究中，针对HPV阴性头颈部鳞状细胞癌（HNSCC），我们结合了生理性三维基质包埋细胞模型和患者来源类器官的研究，并整合多组学分析、生物信息学和人工智能，以揭示重塑染色质以驱动癌症的整合素效应信号网络。在12种α/β1整合素受体中，α7整合素（ITGA7）被鉴定为组蛋白翻译后修饰的最强调节因子，与基因转录和染色质可及性的显著变化相关。通过CRISPR/Cas9敲除和RNA干扰独立实现的ITGA7缺失，降低了AURKA位点的染色质可及性，并下调了以AURKA为中心的转录程序。机制上，磷酸化蛋白质组学揭示了ITGA7缺失后MAPK和PI3K/AKT依赖性信号传导的显著抑制，同时伴随细胞周期和细胞存活的功能损伤。在所有分析中，基于机器学习的特征选择一致地将AURKA提名为主要下游节点，且肿瘤ITGA7表达以非线性方式分层患者总生存期。总之，这些发现确立了α7整合素作为HPV阴性HNSCC中染色质可及性和基因转录的关键共调节因子，通过以AURKA为中心的轴发挥作用，该轴将黏附信号传导与细胞周期控制和患者生存联系起来，并提名AURKA——可潜在靶向临床Aurora-A抑制剂如alisertib——作为当前不可成药ITGA7下游的可操作治疗节点。
